definition: Minimax (sometimes Minmax, MM or saddle point) is a decision rule used in artificial intelligence, decision theory, combinatorial game theory, statistics, and philosophy for minimizing the possible loss for a worst case (maximum loss) scenario.
details: When dealing with gains, it is referred to as "maximin" – to maximize the minimum gain. Originally formulated for several-player zero-sum game theory, covering both the cases where players take alternate moves and those where they make simultaneous moves, it has also been extended to more complex games and to general decision-making in the presence of uncertainty.

explainer.lead: Minimax is a decision rule for minimizing the possible loss in a worst-case scenario. It underpins decision-making in AI, decision theory, statistics and game theory where uncertainty or adversarial play is involved.

tiers.eli5: You choose the option whose worst outcome is least bad, assuming the other side plays against you.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for adversarial and zero-sum decisions, including games with alternating or simultaneous moves. A pitfall is that it optimizes for worst-case outcomes, which can be overly cautious when the worst case is unlikely.
tiers.paperLevel: The maximin value is vi_ = max over ai of min over a−i of vi(ai, a−i), where i is the player of interest, ai its action and a−i all other players' actions; it originated for several-player zero-sum games and has been extended to general decision-making under uncertainty.

explainer.example: A player picks the action whose worst possible value, given all opponents' responses, is as high as possible.
